text.p: Morgan Stockbroking Ltd recommended sugar and building products giant CSR Ltd as a buy, reflecting potential benefits emerging from a recovery in the Australian housing sector.
"With early positive signs now emerging in the Australian housing sector, we expect operating conditions will improve," Morgan analysts said in a report.
CSR's construction materials activities in Australia accounted for 68 percent of CSR's assets, 26 percent in the United States and the balance in Asia and New Zealand, Morgan said.
"The company's prime aim is to build an international building products company, focused on Australia, America and Asia," the Morgan report said.
"In sugar, CSR is building on a strong market position in a rapidly growing raw sugar industry. Aluminium is an investment in two low-cost efficient assets," Morgan said.
CSR's A$3 billion capital expenditure programme was almost complete, the report said.
"The main task for CSR is to improve its return on assets by divesting surplus assets and non-core operations.
"American Aggregates has been sold and timber, aluminium and sugar could arguably be divested," the Morgan analysts said.
Morgan forecast CSR would report its net profit for the year ended March 31, 1997 had dropped to A$229 million from a reported $330.8 million in 1995/96.
CSR will unveil its results in May.
CSR's share price at the time of the report was A$4.83 but by 0540 GMT (3.40 p.m.) on Monday it had fallen to A$4.72.
